newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan business leader urges stock market reforms.
newsitem.headline: Japan business leader urges stock market reforms.

text.p: A top Japanese business leader on Thursday urged the government to take swift measures to invigorate the stock market, such as scrapping taxes on securities transactions and deregulating brokerage commissions.

Shoichiro Toyoda, chairman of the powerful business lobby Keidanren, or Japan Federation of Economic Organisations, also told reporters in Osaka that Japan must not overreact to the stock market's movements.
Japan's closely watched Nikkei stock average has fallen sharply in recent weeks.
Toyoda said Japan was the only country with a securities transaction tax and that it would be appropriate to abolish it.
He also said Japan's economic recovery was spreading, with corporate profits improving and capital spending increasing, even at small companies. He added that the economy was not likely to decline.
